description: Layer 1 trigger pack for large feature implementation orchestration: persist canonical state, split work into phased worker packets, resolve blockers, and manage acceptance across manual worker sessions.

shouldTrigger.prompt: This feature is too big for one coding session. Orchestrate the implementation into phases, worker packets, and review gates.
shouldTrigger.reason: Explicit request for phased implementation orchestration rather than direct coding or design.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Use /orchestrate for team invite approvals. I need a state file, the first worker packet, and a clean return protocol for blockers.
shouldTrigger.reason: Explicit invocation of the orchestration skill with the canonical markdown file workflow.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Break this subscription recovery initiative into implementation phases and write the input files I can hand to separate agent sessions.
shouldTrigger.reason: Manual worker-session packetization is a direct orchestrate trigger.

shouldTrigger.prompt: I already have the feature design. Now I need an orchestrator to own delivery, blockers, and acceptance across several sessions.
shouldTrigger.reason: Positions the task after design and before implementation, with persistent coordination needs.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Create a persistent orchestration plan for rolling out delegated workspace access across API, admin, mobile, and notifications.
shouldTrigger.reason: Cross-surface rollout with persistent planning and coordination should route to orchestrate.

shouldTrigger.prompt: I need the main agent to stay as orchestrator, keep a markdown state file, and respond to worker blocker files as they come in.
shouldTrigger.reason: Explicit persistent orchestrator mode with markdown blocker handling.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Set up a feature delivery loop for invite approvals: write orchestrator.state.md, phase packets, and resume files for future blocker handling.
shouldTrigger.reason: Matches the exact markdown protocol owned by orchestrate.

shouldTrigger.prompt: This rollout is too risky to just code through. I want phased implementation packets, deep review gates, and one orchestrator state file.
shouldTrigger.reason: Risk-managed delivery orchestration with explicit review gates is a strong orchestrate signal.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Plan the implementation program for our permissions rewrite and give me the exact launcher prompt each worker session should use.
shouldTrigger.reason: Launcher-prompt generation for worker sessions is specific to orchestrate.

shouldTrigger.prompt: Read the existing packet output file, accept or reject it, update the orchestration state, and produce the next worker input file.
shouldTrigger.reason: Ingesting worker outputs and generating the next packet is core orchestrate behavior.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Audit our team invite approvals end to end: gaps, trust issues, cross-surface problems, and roadmap priorities.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /feature-audit: broad diagnosis and prioritization, not implementation orchestration.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Design how team invite approvals should work before implementation. Compare approaches and turn the winner into a spec.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /feature-design: deciding how the feature should work comes before orchestration.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Find the real bug in our invite acceptance flow, prove the root cause, fix it, and add a regression test.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /deep-fix: one bug plus verified fix, not a feature delivery program.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Plan a safe refactor for extracting provider billing logic into separate modules without breaking the repo midway.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /refactor-plan: structural sequencing rather than feature delivery orchestration.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Generate unit tests for src/invites/service.ts and match the repo's Vitest style.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /generate-tests: targeted test generation request.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Pressure-test this rollout proposal for invite approvals before we commit to it.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /pressure-test: challenge one proposal, not coordinate the entire implementation program.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Run a deep review of this branch with security, correctness, and architecture lenses before release.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /deep-review: review workflow, not feature orchestration.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: Analyze this diff and give me the deploy checklist: migrations, env vars, workers, and breaking changes.
Create a draft PR for the current branch with the right title, summary, and affected areas.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Routes to /create-pr: PR generation is downstream of orchestration.

shouldNotTrigger.prompt: The change is tiny: update the invite-expiry copy and one button label, then commit it.
shouldNotTrigger.reason: Small direct changes should not trigger orchestration at all.
